summary: This benchmark investigates whether small code and general-purpose LLMs track indentation depth by reasoning over test assertion outputs when all four indentation levels produce syntactically valid code. Evaluating Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B across 256 Python repair problems, the authors show that both models fail to condition on assertion values, instead defaulting to rigid structural priors (achieving 25.0% and 24.6% accuracy, virtually identical to random/majority guessing). The experimental design is rigorous, statistically grounded with bootstrap confidence intervals, and adheres to a disciplined pre-registered discovery gating protocol.
strengths: Rigorous experimental isolation: all four repair candidates parse and execute cleanly, isolating semantic execution reasoning from syntax-checking shortcuts.
Counterfactual prompt design: problem quartets differ strictly in expected assertion outputs while keeping function templates and public inputs constant.
Exemplary research discipline: adhering strictly to a pre-registered discovery gate threshold (+5.0 points) and halting the pipeline before snooping on held-out splits.
Clear, reproducible quantification of positional bias, revealing that the host model selected 4 spaces 100% of the time and the coding donor kept invariant choices in 59 of 64 quartets.
weaknesses: Evaluated on a narrow model set consisting only of small frozen models (Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B), leaving open how larger frontier models or reasoning-tuned variants behave.
Constrained strictly to single-token fill-in-the-middle logit ranking without testing whether scratchpad or chain-of-thought prompting would allow the models to trace the execution.
No runnable supporting repository was attached with the submission, restricting the evaluation badge to text_only.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark to test whether chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting or execution trace scratchpads enable models to resolve the correct indentation depth.
Evaluate instruction-tuned and larger parameter scale models (e.g., 7B and 32B variants) to test if this failure mode is purely a capacity limitation of sub-2B models.
Provide a public artifact repository containing the problem dataset and evaluation harnesses to enable external replication.
